build.note: Read from saved raw captures; no export, no new capture.

question: Where are the hit-quality steps of the damage rule (turret 0.75, body 1, side 1.5, rear 2) stored, at what angles do they apply, and which vehicles use them?

sourceFacts.method: All 20 files under _VehiclesCommon/AngleDamage were decoded and every .ebx in the 54 saved capture roots (31,503 files) was byte-searched for their file GUIDs. The six SimplifiedTank curves are referenced by one file, the schematic PF_Vehicle_GameplayDamageZones_Tank, which was decoded: four damage-zone objects (Class_6f785351), each with a per-face list (Field_12c84a54) naming a curve per face. The same byte search for the schematic's own file GUID lists the files that reference it.

control.description: EA 1.3.1.0 states the four steps; the curves hold 0.75 (Turret), 1.0 (Top), 1.5 (Sides) and 2.0 (Rear). RPG direct product 250 (L3323) x 0.75 / 1.5 / 2 = 188 / 375 / 500: EA's range ends and the operator's 375 side reading already in VEHICLES.md.

sourceFacts.olderCurves: AngleDamageCurve_Tank_*_Shared and IFV_*_Shared (1.0 to 3.2) are still imported directly by the Abrams and CV90 damage-zone files (L3201); they do not reproduce EA's figures.

inference: The hit-quality factors of the damage rule are these curves: turret 0.75 on every side face, body front and top 1.0, body sides 1.5, body rear 2.0, body bottom 2.0.

Side and rear are angle-gated steps, not gradual: the side curve gives 1.5 only between 70 and 110 degrees and the rear curve gives 2.0 only between 55 and 125 degrees; outside those windows both give 1.0. Reading 90 degrees as a square-on hit (the curves are symmetric about 90), a rear hit keeps 2.0 up to 35 degrees off square and a side hit keeps 1.5 up to 20 degrees off square.

The schematic is referenced by the damage-zone files of the Abrams, Leopard, Bradley, CV90 and Gepard, so the same steps are selected for both tanks, both IFVs and the anti-air vehicle. This is stored evidence for the open item of L3334.
The JLTV and Marauder damage zones do not reference the schematic; they import AngleDamageCurve_ArmoredTransport_Shared, a single point (90, 1.0): no angle step on armoured transports.
The body zone has two face lists (set 0 and set 1); set 1 names the Front file (no curve) for every face. What selects between the sets is not decoded.
Faces are stored as numbers 0 to 5; which is front, side, rear, top or bottom is read from the name of the curve each selects, not from a decoded enum.
The front file holds no curve object; the factor 1 for the front is EA's statement, not a stored number.
unresolved: Which of the two body face sets applies, and when. Test: RPG square on a tank's side should remove 375; if it removes 250, set 1 is in use.
Angle windows. Test: RPG on a tank's rear at about 45 degrees off square should remove 250, not 500.
IFV steps. Test: one RPG square on a Bradley's rear should remove 500 of 1000.
Bottom face 2.0: only reachable by mines or explosives under the hull; not compared with any figure.
The AAV7A1 damage-zone file was not among the files that reference the schematic; whether it is saved was not checked.
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.

leads.title: The stored source of EA's 75 / 100 / 150 / 200 percent hit steps: the SimplifiedTank angle curves, selected by both tanks, both IFVs and the Gepard
leads.summary: The four hit steps of the vehicle damage rule are stored in six SimplifiedTank angle curves: turret 0.75, top 1.0, sides 1.5 between 70 and 110 degrees, rear 2.0 between 55 and 125 degrees (1.0 outside those windows), bottom 2.0. One schematic, PF_Vehicle_GameplayDamageZones_Tank, assigns them to faces, and the damage-zone files of the Abrams, Leopard, Bradley, CV90 and Gepard reference it. The JLTV and Marauder use a flat 1.0 curve. 86 raw-offset checks matched.
leads.reopenWhen: An in-game reading at a measured angle, or a decoded selector for the body's two face sets.
leads.statusNote: Stored steps equal EA's four; users found by byte search of 31,503 saved files; face-set selection not decoded.
